s.g: Used to form adjectives from nouns or sometimes other adjectives, often relational (meaning "related to X"). Often equivalent to -al, -ic, or -ical.
Genitive plural desinence of most hard-stem masculine nouns
someone wearing a blouse (usually of French workmen and craftsmen)
deputy prime minister, vice prime minister
to burn down, to burn out, to burn low
to be cold, to feel cold
to innervate (to supply (an organ or part of the body) with nerves)
concrete noun (noun that denotes a tangible thing)
to accumulate, to gather, to amass, to pile up
to devastate, to ravage, to lay waste
to drain someone's spirit, to have a devastating effect (on)
initialism of про́шлого го́да (próšlovo góda, “of last year”)
to develop, to evolve, to advance
merger (the act or process of merging)
fusion (merging of elements into a union)
confluence (point where two rivers or streams meet)
to incite to behave badly, to corrupt
alloy (metal composed of two or more elements, at least one of which is a metal)
to admire, to esteem, to have a good opinion of someone
to honour/honor, to respect, to treat politely
to abide by, to comply, to observe, to not violate
to like, to be fond of
to urge, to exhort, to admonish
second cousin three times removed downwards (second cousin's great grandson).
